title: Fibre-degree superlevel sets for flat locally quasi-finite morphisms
statement: Let $f:Y\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], separated (its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]), and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Assume that for every point $t\in T$ the scheme-theoretic fibre $Y_t=Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-residue-field] is finite over $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Write $Y_t=\operatorname{Spec}B_t$ and $\delta(t)=\dim_{\kappa(t)}B_t$, its finite fibre degree [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]. Then for every integer $d\ge0$ the subset $T_{\ge d}=\{t\in T:\delta(t)\ge d\}$ is open in $T$. Neither a uniform bound on these degrees nor quasi-compactness of $Y$ or $T$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 086R (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-lqf), restricted to morphisms with finite fibres; degree-superlevel open subschemes U_d.

proof.text: Work over an arbitrary affine open $V\subseteq T$, and set $Y_V=f^{-1}(V)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] this is base change along $V\hookrightarrow T$. Flatness, local finite presentation, separatedness and local quasi-finiteness persist by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3), and [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change]. Its fibre at $t\in V$ is the original $Y_t$, by the fibre-product universal property. Thus its degree is $\delta(t)$. It suffices to prove openness inside each $V$, since these opens cover $T$.

Let $W\subseteq Y_V$ be any quasi-compact open, including the empty open, and put $h_W:W\to V$. The affine scheme $V$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1) makes $h_W$ quasi-compact. It is locally quasi-finite by [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens], hence quasi-finite by [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc]. Flatness restricts because the local rings and their structural maps at a source point are unchanged; local finite presentation restricts by shrinking a presenting affine neighbourhood to a principal open $D(g)$ inside $W$: its algebra is presented by adjoining $z$ with relation $gz-1$ [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The diagonal of $h_W$ is the base change of the diagonal of $Y_V\to V$ along $W\times_V W\to Y_V\times_VY_V$. It is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], hence $h_W$ is separated.

For $t\in V$, the fibre $(W)_t$ is the open subscheme of $Y_t$ cut out by $W$, by the open fibre-product identification [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim] write $Y_t=\operatorname{Spec}B_t$ with $B_t$ finite-dimensional over $k=\kappa(t)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] with the local ring $R=k$ and maximal ideal zero: $|Y_t|$ is finite discrete. Thus $(W)_t$ and its complement $C_t$ are open, and both are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-affine]. Sheaf gluing on the disjoint open cover gives a $k$-algebra isomorphism $B_t\cong\Gamma((W)_t,\mathcal O)\times\Gamma(C_t,\mathcal O)$. In particular each factor is finite-dimensional and its dimension is at most $\dim_k B_t$ (each embeds linearly by putting zero in the other factor). By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $(W)_t$ is finite over $k$. Write $\delta_W(t)=\dim_k\Gamma((W)_t,\mathcal O)$; then $0\le\delta_W(t)\le\delta(t)$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fp-qf-stratification] to $h_W$ to obtain closed $Z_{-1}=\varnothing\subseteq Z_0\subseteq\cdots$ and strata $S_r=Z_r\setminus Z_{r-1}$. Its universal property, tested on $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to V$, says that $t\in S_r$ exactly when $\delta_W(t)=r$. Here a finite $k$-scheme of degree $r$ is finite locally free of degree $r$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]: choose a basis of its finite-dimensional algebra; it is a free $k$-module, and the relations $x_ix_j=\sum_k c_{ijk}x_k$ and $1=\sum_i u_ix_i$ from its multiplication table give a finite algebra presentation: they reduce every polynomial to a linear combination of the $x_i$, whose images are a basis. The zero algebra is presented by $(1)$. Conversely the defining degree condition gives that dimension. Because the strata partition $V$, for $d\ge1$ the subset $\{t:\delta_W(t)\ge d\}$ equals $V\setminus Z_{d-1}$ and is open. For $d=0$ it is $V$.

Every fibre $Y_t$ has finitely many underlying points, as proved in step 3. Choose an affine open neighbourhood in $Y_V$ of each such point and let $W$ be their finite union; this is quasi-compact since affine schemes are quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. For an empty fibre choose $W=\varnothing$. Then $(W)_t=Y_t$ as open subschemes: an open subscheme containing every point is the whole scheme, with the same restricted structure sheaf. Consequently $\delta_W(t)=\delta(t)$. No neighbourhood of the entire source, nor a bound valid for all fibres, was chosen.

For each $d\ge0$, step 3 gives inclusion of every $\{t\in V:\delta_W(t)\ge d\}$ into $\{t\in V:\delta(t)\ge d\}$, and step 5 gives the reverse inclusion in their union. Hence $$\{t\in V:\delta(t)\ge d\}=\bigcup_{W\subseteq Y_V\ \mathrm{quasi\text{-}compact\ open}}\{t\in V:\delta_W(t)\ge d\}.$$ Each set on the right is open by step 4, so the union is open. Taking the union over the affine open cover of $T$ proves the assertion. The index is a set of open subsets of the underlying set of $Y_V$. This also treats $d=0$, the empty source and the empty base.
